item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commissioner Against Corruption reviewed the operation and effectiveness of the Whistleblowers Protection Act 1993 at the Attorney-General’s request.
item.support:
The Attorney-General has requested me to conduct that review and report to 
him.

item.text: The review considered protected disclosures, reporting pathways, confidentiality, victimisation remedies and oversight within the state’s integrity framework.
item.support:
That WBL include an offence for disclosing the identity 
of a person who has made a public interest disclosure

item.text: The Commissioner concluded that the Act should be replaced because it was not fulfilling its purpose of encouraging disclosures and protecting those who made them.
item.section: WBP Act – Amendment or Repeal and Re-enactment?
item.support:
I do 
not think it is fulfilling its primary objective of facilitating disclosure and 
providing protections for those who make disclosures.

item.text: The Commissioner made 30 recommendations addressing replacement legislation, investigation duties, reporting channels, whistleblower protection and oversight.
item.support:
That WBL provide an obligation, subject to appropriate 
exceptions, to investigate disclosures.

item.quote:
The WBP Act be repealed and a new Act be 
substituted that clearly addresses the four fundamental issues relevant to 
whistleblowing and the further recommendations mentioned in this review.
